correctness.rationale: The three quadratic square classes over F3(t) have six disjoint geometric branch points and give a connected smooth tame (Z/2)^3 cover of degree eight and genus five. Character eigenspaces give three explicit genus-one quotients and one genus-two quotient and a 2-primary isogeny. Exhaustive base-field sums give quotient point counts E_i(F3)=4, E_i(F9)=16, H(F3)=4 and H(F9)=6, hence L_E=1+3T² and L_H=1-2T²+9T⁴ by Weil functional equations. The actual standalone verifier computes X(F3)=4, X(F9)=24, X(F27)=28, X(F81)=56 and separately enumerates the original projective three-quadric model over F3 and F9. The Cartier–Manin matrix of H is invertible, whereas each trace-zero elliptic factor is supersingular, proving rank two, a-number three and the stated Newton slopes under a prime-to-three isogeny. Irreducibility of the genus-two degree-four Frobenius characteristic polynomial proves simplicity over F3. All-extension counts follow from the proven zeta, not extrapolation from finite experiments.

originality.rationale: The exact characteristic-three Weil numerator, the three supersingular elliptic factors, ordinary simple surface, 3-rank and a-number of the fixed rational model are not printed in the inspected primary texts. Swinarski 2016 gives the same canonical equations over C (no claim of novelty for them), while Kudo–Harashita 2021 reports exact Weil polynomials only for the 32-point F9 threshold; this curve has 24 F9 points. Kudo–Harashita 2022 studies hyperelliptic/trigonal models instead of the stated smooth three-quadric model. Known general character/idempotent splittings supply methodology but not this numeric Frobenius calculation. Literature search is not proof of novelty: an older specialized 2011 genus-five bielliptic paper was not accessible in full, and unindexed arithmetic tables may overlap.

value.rationale: The fixed Wiman model is an exceptional highly symmetric genus-five complete intersection, and its characteristic-three reduction lies in the same natural arithmetic genus-five setting that motivated recent exact F3/F9 searches. The exact zeta function over every extension and prime-to-three Jacobian decomposition distinguish its mixed Newton slopes, identify a simple ordinary abelian surface factor, and provide a controlled nonordinary 3-rank two/a-number three example not implied by generic geometry alone. This is substantive arithmetic data for a distinguished algebraic curve, not a random coefficient slice or a tiny increment in a benchmark bound; it is also explicitly not presented as an optimal-point record.
